_doc: Build scenarios of the DPV1 estate. classify_scenarios.py assigns one scenario and any number of modifiers to each source dataset (S-*) and data product (D-*) from what its DPV1 code does. Each entry says how it is built, which tools exist, and what is still open. Read by classify_scenarios.py (catalogs and scenarios.json) and the hub page. status: ready = built and reviewed in a pilot; partial = built, some part not verified in Fabric; gap = the build does not cover it yet (backlog).

S-DB-FULL.title: Database source, full load
S-DB-FULL.detect: A database linked service (Oracle, SQL Server, Azure SQL, PostgreSQL...) and no watermark read in the DPV1 pipelines. Catalog flags such as isIncLoad may exist but are unused.
build: S1 catalog view from the DPV1 catalog script, Lakehouse LH_SDS_<SRC>
S2 one Copy per catalog row, SELECT * (or the DPV1 per-table query), parquet written once to Files/raw
S3 one loader notebook NB_<SRC>_RAW_TO_DELTA only when DPV1 cleansed in a notebook, else a Copy raw to table; tables load in parallel in one session
S4 master orchestrator, VL_MAIN, schedule documented and not activated

S-DB-INC.title: Database source, incremental load
S-DB-INC.detect: A database linked service and the DPV1 pipelines read a watermark (WatermarkParam, WatermarkVal, isFullLoad).
build: As S-DB-FULL, plus a watermark table in the catalog warehouse
S2 extracts changes since the watermark minus 1 day
S3 MERGE on the key columns, newest row wins, delete logs and history tables
S4 master updates the watermark only for tables that loaded
open: Built and reviewed, not yet run end to end in Fabric (B46)

S-REST-FULL.title: REST API, full load
S-REST-FULL.detect: A REST linked service and no watermark in the request.
build: S1 catalog view (one row per API path)
S2 Copy per row lands the JSON pages as delivered in Files/landing (DPV1 pagination rules copied)
S3 NB_<SRC>_FLATTEN writes flattened parquet to Files/raw, then the loader writes the tables
S4 master, VL_MAIN, connection per API
open: The raw layout of API sources with a landing zone (B56) is not settled

S-REST-INC.title: REST API, incremental load
S-REST-INC.detect: A REST linked service and the request carries a watermark (in the URL or a parameter, different for every API).
build: As S-REST-FULL
S1 the catalog parser reads every DPV1 catalog layout (multi-line values, column lists)
S2 the DPV1 request is copied to 2-config/migration/request-urls/<SRC>.json (item().WatermarkVal => item().WatermarkNow) and used as relativeUrl; the Lookup returns the live watermark
S4 the master updates the watermark of the tables that loaded
open: Request derived from the catalog row for ONEGBS, EPTW and ECOSYS_COSTCONTROL; SERVICENOW and OCTOPASS build it from pipeline parameters or variables: write it in "override" of the request file. Not run in Fabric (B46)

S-FILES-FULL.title: File source, full load
S-FILES-FULL.detect: SFTP, FTP, blob, file share, S3, Azure Files or HTTP files, and no watermark.
build: S1 catalog view (one row per file pattern)
S2 Copy per row lands the files as delivered in Files/landing
S3 NB_<SRC>_FLATTEN converts csv, Excel, xml or json to parquet in Files/raw, then the loader
S4 master, VL_MAIN

S-FILES-INC.title: File source, incremental load
S-FILES-INC.detect: File source and the DPV1 pipelines filter on the modified date or a watermark.
build: As S-FILES-FULL, with modifiedDatetimeStart set from the watermark for incremental rows
open: Not run end to end in Fabric

S-POOL.title: Source is the DPV1 dedicated pool
S-POOL.detect: The only linked service is a Synapse SQL pool (AzureSqlDW): the pipeline copies data out of the pool, for example an offload to SPOT.
build: Usually not a source: the data is produced by a data product. Confirm with the owner whether to drop it or replace it by the product's Warehouse tables

S-MANUAL.title: No external source found
S-MANUAL.detect: No external linked service or copy source was detected. The data comes from another DPV1 mechanism (metabase, manual load).
build: Assess by hand from the DPV1 objects listed in the framing, then choose another scenario
open: Needs a human look before framing

M-MIXED.title: Two kinds of input in one source
M-MIXED.how: Database plus files in one source (GAIA: Oracle and SharePoint CSV). file-inputs/<SRC>.json lists the files (one catalog row each, ConnectionKey files); S2 has a second Lookup, ForEach and Copy; FLATTEN converts the file rows and passes the database rows on; the loader reads each row from its own raw folder; the contract lists the file tables. Other combinations (files plus REST, several file groups) are still manual.

M-SWITCH-QUERIES.title: Per-table queries in a Switch
M-SWITCH-QUERIES.how: Extracted from the DPV1 Switch into 2-config/migration/extract-queries/<SRC>.json and returned by the catalog Lookup as ExtractQuery.

M-PAGINATION.title: REST pagination
M-PAGINATION.how: Pagination rules copied from the DPV1 Copy.

M-EXCEL.title: Excel files
M-EXCEL.how: Landed as delivered, converted sheet by sheet to parquet in the FLATTEN notebook.

M-WEB-AUTH.title: Token or secret fetched by a Web activity
M-WEB-AUTH.how: Replaced by a Fabric connection. The Key Vault secret name stays in the connection sheet; no secret in the repo.

M-SHAREPOINT-GRAPH.title: SharePoint through Microsoft Graph
M-SHAREPOINT-GRAPH.how: DPV1 gets a Graph token with a Web activity. The Copy uses an HTTP connection (VL_MAIN <SRC>_HTTP_SERVER_CONN_ID) with relativeUrl root:/<folder>/<file>:/content; the service principal and the connector are to confirm in Fabric.

M-NOTEBOOK-CLEANSING.title: DPV1 cleansed in a notebook
M-NOTEBOOK-CLEANSING.how: The cleansing rules are read from the legacy notebooks and generated into one loader notebook.

M-DATAFLOW.title: Mapping data flows
M-DATAFLOW.how: Converted to Spark notebooks (skill-dataflow-to-notebook in DPV2).

M-REST-INCREMENTAL.title: REST API with a watermark
M-REST-INCREMENTAL.how: See S-REST-INC: the DPV1 request is carried with the live watermark.

M-MODELING-IN-SOURCE.title: Modeling notebooks listed in the source dataset scope
M-MODELING-IN-SOURCE.how: Notebooks such as *_DIM or *_MODEL build the BI model, which is data product work (INTELEX lists about 20 in the source dataset). Confirm at framing and move them to the data product.

M-FLAGS-UNUSED.title: Catalog flags that DPV1 never reads
M-FLAGS-UNUSED.how: The catalog marks tables incremental but the pipeline loads in full. Keep full, as DPV1 does, and ask the owner.

D-LDW.title: Modeling in serverless LDW views
D-LDW.detect: LDW views (CREATE VIEW [LDW]... or SP_CREATE_* procedures whose body is the view) between the INP views and the dedicated pool.
build: D1 extract the embedded SQL of the pipelines (extract_scope_code.py)

D2 convert_serverless_sql.py: SP_CREATE_* procedures and LDW / OUT views become Warehouse views reading LH_INP_SDS_<SRC> tables (contract names), SP_TRAN_* loaders read the OUT views, STG and CETAS dropped, K3 fixes applied
K2 dacpac_retarget.py --flat 3-build/_work/d2-converted-sql places them; K3 lint must show 0 blocking; K4 dotnet build (SDK 8)
D3 input Lakehouse with one shortcut per table the code reads
D4 process pipeline from d2-load-order.json: dimensions in parallel, then facts
D5 equivalence: counts and checksums per table
open: Built and lint-clean on GAIA (67 views, 48 loaders, 0 unmapped reads); dotnet build not run (the machine has SDK 10 only), D4 pipelines and D5 tests are written by hand
Views with ORDER BY are listed in the D2 notes and need a TOP or the ORDER BY removed

D-PROC.title: Modeling in dedicated-pool procedures
D-PROC.detect: Stored procedures in the dedicated pool do the transformation; pipelines call them in batches.
build: D1 extract what the repo holds
K1 to K4 DACPAC from the code, or from the live pool when procedures are called but not defined in the repo
D3 warehouse and input Lakehouse
D4 batches in the DPV1 order, parallel inside a batch
open: Procedures that exist only in the pool need a DACPAC extract or a login (see dacpac_source)

D-COPY.title: Copy-through (OUT to STG to DW to DM)
D-COPY.detect: Config-driven Copy activities move tables into the pool; little or no logic in the pool.
build: D1 extract the embedded SQL; D2 pool_read.py ddl (live pool DDL is the truth), convert_serverless_sql.py, d2_assemble_flat.py: silver tables, INT_SILV views from the OUT views, one SP_LOAD per table, the [INP_<SRC>] input views
K2 dacpac_retarget.py --flat 3-build/_work/d2-flat --schema-map ... --gold-views: 1-input, 2-intermediate, 3-processing, 4-output, gold views over silver
D3 resolve_upstream.py then build_input_lakehouse.py, build_warehouse.py, create_variable_library.py
D4 build_process_pipeline.py: master and child pipelines
D6 review_scope.py and deploy_preflight.py check: no failure; deploy_preflight.py runbook for the order of the deployment
open: Built, reviewed and published for RMA; not yet synced in Fabric. The DACPAC is built by the Azure DevOps pipeline (.NET 8)
Confirm that nothing reads the DW tables (Q06)

D-DATAFLOW.title: Modeling in mapping data flows
D-DATAFLOW.detect: Mapping data flows in the pipelines do the transformation.
build: Dataflows become Spark notebooks (skill-dataflow-to-notebook), pool code through the DACPAC
open: No converter in this repo yet

D-SPARK.title: Modeling in Spark notebooks
D-SPARK.detect: Spark notebooks named *_MODEL, *_DIM, *_FACT or *_OUT_COPY do the transformation; the pool is at most a copy target.
build: Notebooks converted to Fabric notebooks (skill-pyspark-synapse-to-fabric), writing to the Lakehouse

D-SERVERLESS-VIEWS.title: Serverless views only
D-SERVERLESS-VIEWS.detect: A serverless database with views (business-user databases), no dedicated pool.
build: Views move to the Lakehouse SQL endpoint or a Warehouse over the input Lakehouse; no loads
open: Target (SQL endpoint or Warehouse) to decide with the owner

D-NONE.title: Nothing to build in a Warehouse
D-NONE.detect: No dedicated pool objects, views or notebooks in the scope.
build: Confirm with the owner that the product is a source-side consumer only, then close it as dropped or handled by the source dataset

M-LDW-SP-CREATE.title: LDW and OUT views written as SP_CREATE_* procedures
M-LDW-SP-CREATE.how: The procedure body is the view: convert_serverless_sql.py writes CREATE VIEW [ldw|out].[<NAME>] (the batch number of the DPV1 name is kept in the notes).

M-LDW-DIRECT-VIEWS.title: LDW views written as CREATE VIEW
M-LDW-DIRECT-VIEWS.how: Extracted from the embedded SQL and placed in 2-intermediate in dependency order.

M-OUT-VIEWS.title: OUT views feed the load
M-OUT-VIEWS.how: Kept as views in 2-intermediate; the DW or DM tables are loaded from them by set-based procedures.

M-CETAS.title: CETAS copies to the lake
M-CETAS.how: Dropped: the Warehouse reads the Lakehouse directly.

M-SPOT-COPY-BACK.title: Warehouse copied back to SPOT
M-SPOT-COPY-BACK.how: Dropped when the consumers read the Warehouse. Ask who reads the SPOT copy.

M-MANY-SOURCES.title: More than two source datasets
M-MANY-SOURCES.how: Every source needs its contract before the product starts.

M-DDL-EMBEDDED.title: Table DDL inside pipeline scripts
M-DDL-EMBEDDED.how: Unwrapped from EXEC('...') into object files by extract_scope_code.py.

M-DDL-IN-SCRIPTS.title: Table DDL in SQL scripts
M-DDL-IN-SCRIPTS.how: Read from the Synapse SQL scripts.

M-POOL-ONLY-CODE.title: Procedures called but not defined in the repo
M-POOL-ONLY-CODE.how: The code exists only in the live dedicated pool: extract a DACPAC from it (SqlPackage) or ask for the project.

M-FRAMEWORK-PROCS.title: Shared framework procedures
M-FRAMEWORK-PROCS.how: catalog.sp_common_updatewatermark, sp_meta_out_cetas and similar are replaced by the Fabric catalog and watermark, not migrated.

dacpac_source.scripts-complete: Every procedure the pipelines call is defined in the repo: build the DACPAC from the code (wf-4 K1 option 3).
dacpac_source.pool-required: Procedures are called but not defined in the repo: ask for the DACPAC or database project, or a read login to extract it from the dedicated pool (SqlPackage /Action:Extract).
dacpac_source.ddl-only: Table DDL is in the repo, no procedures are called: build the DACPAC from the DDL.
